sections.text: I am not visible to all, for I am enveloped by the illusion of Phenomenon. This deluded world does not know Me as the Unborn and the Imperishable.
I know, O Arjuna, all beings in the past, the present and the future; but they do not know Me.
O brave Arjuna! Man lives in a fairy world, deceived by the glamour of opposite sensations, infatuated by desire and aversion.

We have been discussing Chapter 7, Gnana Vignana Yoga, the Yoga of Knowledge and Wisdom -- knowledge about the Supreme Self, contemplating on which we can attain wisdom. In this chapter, from verses 4 through 7, Bhagavan gave a thumbnail sketch of who the Lord is and what to meditate upon. First, he said his manifest Prakriti is Eightfold, available to us for perception through our senses -- everything we can think of, see, touch, and feel.
All experiences of body, mind, and intellect are part of His manifested Prakriti. But then he said there is also His higher Prakriti, the para Prakriti. In other words, that which is not available to us for cognition through our senses.
Therefore its called unmanifest -- not available to thinking through my mind, thinking through my intellect, or perceiving through my senses. The lower Prakriti is what I can interact with. The higher I cannot perceive.
But that higher is the basis of all manifestation, without which the world which you and I know will not exist. If Im not conscious about my world, does the world exist? It only exists because Im aware of it. The known only exists when the Knower is there.
Because the Knower is there, the world of known things and beings exists. So therefore Bhagavan said, my Higher Prakriti is the one which is stringing all these manifestations together. What you perceive, what I perceive, what he perceives, what she perceives -- when you put all perception together, it is a world of beings.
Thats His real nature. So from verses 4 through 7, weve seen the identity of the Lord, the Supreme, our Self, and how to contemplate on it. And then Bhagavan said you can perceive Him through anything which is the essence of anything.
Brilliance in the brilliant. Used to say, I am the kick in whiskey. What is whiskey if there is no kick in it? It may look like whiskey, it may taste like whiskey, but if there is no kick, its not whiskey. That which makes things and beings what they are -- that is who I am.
Then he said that people who have no discriminating intellect to pursue this will never pursue it, never want to think about it. But there are people who are pursuing an understanding of the very nature of the self and trying to get over their limitations. We have seen four types of devotees: Artah, Jijnasu, Artharthi, and Gnani.
The Gnani is very close to me. He has come close to understanding what the self is all about. To Arjuna: therefore, become a Gnani.
Therefore, pursue the path of knowledge which makes you realize who you are. And then he also said that in our delusion, we sometimes think the unmanifest comes into manifestation. But the unmanifest never manifests -- we only feel it has.
Bhagavan Vedvyasa makes this point very clear here, because we have all this fighting about different religions. We say, Our Bhagavan manifested as Krishna. Yours manifested as Christ, but mine is greater than yours. The very first ignorance is thinking the unmanifest comes into manifest.
The unmanifest will never come into manifestation. Anyone who has used his intellect knows: every religion says God is omnipresent, omniscient, omnipotent. Then how can your God be different than mine? If my God is omnipresent, there is no room for another God.
Knowing this, why are we fighting about whose God is greater? Abuddhayah -- without using my intellect, I think the unmanifest God comes into manifestation as an incarnation, a prophet, a sage. Param bhavam ajanantah. They are not aware of my real nature.
My real nature is Avyayam -- immutable. Bhagavan created this world out of His own self because He has no other material available. Did He ever mutate into this world? He never mutated into this world.
Therefore, one who does not know that His nature is immutable -- he is the one who is fighting about it. There is nothing higher than that. There is nothing beyond His existence.
If you take Him out, nothing remains. If you put everything together, there is nothing but Him alone. But see, thats not available to all of us.
To perceive my own self is what Im trying to understand. How can it be that difficult? It is difficult because: Na aham prakasah sarvasya yogamaya samavritah. I am not available to all because my real nature is veiled by Yoga Maya.
This Yoga Maya, which creates the world of plurality out of these three gunas, confuses us so we cant see His real nature. Mudho ayam na abhijanati loko mam ajam avyayam. Deluded by that Yoga Maya, I do not recognize its very nature, which is unborn and immutable.
That is where our whole problem starts -- our sorrows and limitations. This Yoga Maya is the power with which He created this universe. The perception of plurality is because of this Yoga Maya.
It is like when Im dreaming: out of my own mental power, I create my own world and delude myself. I create my own world, but I -- the waker -- remain immutable. In that dream, the waking self remains unchanged.
I remain Ajah in my dream. I never take birth as Bill Gates, but I feel in my dream that Im Bill Gates. So he said, that is not available to all.
Nobody will ever know it. But this is not a statement to discourage us -- it is a statement for us to contemplate on. He said it is available to those who contemplate His real nature and cross over this Maya, who see beyond it -- therefore the word Divya Drishti.
I have one perspective about this world right now, and I can change my perspective when I get greater knowledge. Before I came to Richmond, I had one perspective. I thought, Oh, Richmond is a very conservative southern town. An old-boy network type of town.
It seemed so far away in the south from Washington D.C. Where I used to live -- its only 100 miles, but I thought it was way down in the deep south. My company kept telling me, You need to move to Richmond. Until I came here and recognized this is a pretty cosmopolitan town.
The more knowledge I get, the better my perspective becomes. It becomes more encompassing. So Bhagavan said, one who does not have this perspective will not know my nature.
We will need a Divya Drishti to see His real nature in totality. Mudha means one who has not yet developed that perspective -- who doesnt yet see the totality of the Lords nature. Therefore, we learned from verses 4 through 7 how to see Him in totality.
There is nothing separate from anything else. We are not islands by ourselves. We are connected in a way that we can never separate ourselves from each other.
You cant have this class without any one of you. We need all of you, including myself, to have this class. But if I miss that perspective, I am a Mudha.
A father cannot be a father without a son or daughter. A daughter cannot be a daughter without father and mother. This interdependence we have right from birth is what we miss because of our ego.
Then we say, I am a self-made man. You couldnt even breathe on your own. So Bhagavan said: Vedaham samatitani vartamanani cha Arjuna bhavishyani cha bhutani. I know all beings of past, present, and future. But mam tu veda na kashchana -- no one knows me. Its a real hide-and-seek game. The one at the top, with a greater perspective, sees everything, but we cant see Him.
He knows everyone. Its like Krishna saying, I know all beings in the past, present, and future, but no one knows me. Its like the space in Henrico County claiming tomorrow, I know all the buildings in Henrico County past, present, and future. Because no building is possible without the inherent ingredient of space in it. From spaces perspective, no building is unknown.
From a buildings perspective, I only know the conditioned space. Therefore I think Im limited. I have birth, I have death.
I dont know what is the real nature of the space. I think the nature of the space is the room. So all of us, as soon as we take this identification, we forget the real nature of ourselves and take the identification of the conditioning.
But from the perspective of consciousness -- the same consciousness in me as in you, as in him, as was in my father, my grandfather, my ancestors 5,000 years ago -- the same consciousness. Therefore, from consciousnesss perspective, it knew all beings in the past, present, and future. Because it never changed; it remained what it is.
Beings and their conditioning came and went and will come and go, but the inherent ingredient, the entity which makes it all possible, remains the same. So we know God is omnipresent. None of us somehow doubt it.
That which is omnipresent, by its very nature, becomes omniscient. If I am all-pervading in this space, I know everything about it. So Bhagavan is omnipresent and therefore omniscient.
But from a narrow perspective, if I try to understand Bhagavan, it will never be possible. Therefore He says, Mam tu veda na kashchana. Because we try to personify Him as a limited entity.
Therefore, North Indian Rama looks North Indian and South Indian Rama looks South Indian. The artist paints it in his imagination. We see Bhagavan in our imagination.
We put all our conditioning on Him. Therefore Bhagavan says, No one knows me. We have to cross over these limitations of our mind and intellect. Therefore its called transcendental meditation.
Iccha dvesha samutthena dvandva mohena Bharata. What creates this confusion? Iccha and Dvesha -- likes and dislikes. Sarvabhutani sammoham sarge yanti parantapa.
All beings are deluded from the very moment of birth by likes and dislikes. Right from birth, the little baby knows what is comfortable and what is not. As soon as something is not comfortable -- the diaper is wet -- it starts crying.
It has already taken on that conditioning. Per our scriptures, that baby has taken its conditioning -- because of past Vasanas, that body is taken. I take this particular state of existence -- thats what I wanted to experience.
Why do I go to concerts and not to boxing matches? Thats what I want to experience. Thats why I go to concerts, not wrestling matches. The one who goes to wrestling matches -- tell him to go to the opera! So you have taken on your conditioning based on what you like.
Now you divide your world into the world you like and the world you dont like -- the world of your physical existence and the world of your emotions involved with your thinking.

I am not visible to all, for I am enveloped by the illusion of Yoga-Maya. This verse reveals why the spiritual search feels like hide-and-seek. The Divine is not hiding from us; we are veiled from seeing what is already everywhere present. Like someone searching for their glasses while wearing them, we seek what we already are. Today, instead of trying to find God or truth, try relaxing the very effort to seek. In moments of pure presence, without agenda or grasping, what remains?
I know all beings in the past, the present and the future; but they do not know Me. From the perspective of space, all rooms are known because space pervades all rooms. But from the perspective of a single room, space seems confined to those four walls. Your consciousness, which seems limited to your body and mind, is actually the same universal consciousness that pervades all beings across all time. Todays exercise: When you meet someone, briefly consider that the awareness looking out from their eyes is the same awareness looking out from yours. Only the conditioning, the room, is different.
The root cause of delusion is revealed: Iccha-dvesha-samutthena, born of likes and dislikes. From the moment of birth, we divide the world into what we want and what we reject. This fundamental duality creates all suffering. Today, notice your automatic reactions of attraction and aversion. The morning coffee you crave, the traffic you despise, the praise you seek, the criticism you avoid. Can you observe these preferences without being completely controlled by them? Even brief moments of equanimity, accepting what is without demanding it be different, give a taste of freedom from the dvandvas (pairs of opposites).
